prompt:
Find what the Node.js project officially says about the lifecycle of its LTS releases (how long Active LTS and Maintenance LTS last). Cite the official page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
The Node.js project defines its Long Term Support (LTS) lifecycle through a specific schedule managed by the Release Working Group. According to the official documentation, an LTS release enters an "Active LTS" phase for 12 months, followed by a "Maintenance LTS" phase for 18 months, resulting in a total support period of 30 months from the date the version enters LTS.

SOURCE: https://github.com/nodejs/Release | QUOTE: "Each major active LTS line will be maintained for 12 months after which it will move into Maintenance LTS for a further 18 months." | CLAIM: Active LTS lasts for 12 months and Maintenance LTS lasts for 18 months.
